title: Inside the Free Clinic Caring for Those Who Can’t Afford the Only Hospital in Town
author: Mauricio Rodríguez Pons
content:
The Samaritan Clinic is a small, free clinic serving people without health
insurance in Albany, Georgia. It was created in 2008 to provide care for
people who couldn’t afford medical treatment. More than 15 years later, the
need has changed little. Today, Albany has one of the highest poverty rates in
the state. About 16% of residents are uninsured, nearly double the national
average. And people here pay some of the highest commercial health insurance
rates in the country.

Not far from the Samaritan Clinic is Phoebe Putney Memorial Hospital,
Southwest Georgia’s largest hospital — a nonprofit founded on the principle
that patients should be treated regardless of their ability to pay.

So why do some residents turn to a free clinic for care?  
  
[This short documentary](https://youtu.be/Ia9pWMK9fDQ) is part of “[Sick in a
Hospital Town](https://propublica.org/albany),” a five-part series about why
people in Albany are so sick when the main institution is a hospital. You can
[read](https://projects.propublica.org/albany-georgia-hospital/) and
[listen](https://podcasts.apple.com/us/podcast/sick-in-a-hospital-town-
part-1/id1858752858?i=1000740060363) to it.  
  
[Watch the video here.](https://youtu.be/Ia9pWMK9fDQ)
